tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with concrete trigger phrases like 'why is my AWS Config bill so high', and lists explicit trigger contexts covering both named and unnamed domain requests. It is a single dense paragraph (concise for the scope covered) though on the longer side, it still reads as one coherent unit without redundancy.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize AWS Config spend, or reports an unexpected AWS Config cost or configuration-item increase. Activate on requests like \"why is my AWS Config bill so high\", \"reduce Config costs\"..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is focused on domain-specific procedures (Config billing model, workflow steps, severity definitions, safety boundaries) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. Content is dense with AWS Config-specific facts.
tests.evidence: Configuration items (CIs) are the dominant cost driver — billed per CI recorded.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (API calls, full pricing tables, opportunity check definitions) is offloaded to references/ files and only summarized briefly in the body. No large blocks of detailed data or conditional-branch reference data are embedded in the body.
tests.evidence: For the full charge table, per-mode pricing, and the high-churn reasoning the checks rely on, load references/billing-model.md

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files are linked with markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies the condition or purpose for loading, e.g., when deciding continuous vs daily, or for API call details.
tests.evidence: load references/billing-model.md when you need to decide whether continuous or daily is cheaper for a resource type, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root (references/filename.md format).

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only API safety boundary, compliance tradeoffs, conformance-pack decision tree) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while flexible tasks (report generation approach, scope selection) allow agent judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Never recommend dropping recording below the organization's audit requirements.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple approaches exist (e.g., Cost Explorer vs Athena vs GetDiscoveredResourceCounts), a clear preferred order and default is given with fallbacks noted.
tests.evidence: Prefer Cost Explorer as the dollar signal, use Athena (or GetDiscoveredResourceCounts as an approximate fallback) for CI-driver attribution

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope identification, inventory, cost signal collection, opportunity analysis, validation, reporting) applicable to any AWS Config cost review, not a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to AWS Config cost domain.
tests.evidence: Daily's higher per-CI price is not a reason to avoid it — for high-churn resources, daily's once-per-day cap beats continuous billing every change.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a report and provides an explicit template in assets/, referenced from the body.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body

tests.name: Asset path format

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, matching the required format, and there are no separate detailed sections with mismatched headings.
tests.evidence: - [ ] **Step 1: Identify target scope.** ... - [ ] **Step 2: Inventory the Config setup.**

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check findings for accuracy, compliance tradeoffs, and correctness before presenting the report.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm each estimated saving traces to a cited signal... Drop or re-label any finding that fails these checks.
